messages:
zoe: RFC follow-up - quick design check. I want to formalize an "escape-hatch" and separate 'lane' semantics in the router so rollbacks don't get stuck because of sticky binds. Thoughts?

ira: yes please. Current problem is routers keep sticky mappings for session affinity which pins in-flight work to old variant. We need a minimal contract so controller/arbiter can tell router how to treat existing binds vs new ones.

ben: propose three lane actions: CONTINUE (do nothing), REHOME (route new binds away but let existing finish), and QUIT (stop assigning new and refuse new binds to old variant). Clarify that QUIT still never terminates mid-response.

zoe: agreed. Add a small decision envelope we can sign and publish. Fields: decision_id, tenant, action, drain_until, ttl_secs, confidence, signer_version. Example in RFC.

ira: important: include reason and probe_count so ops can audit "why" a QUIT happened. Also include api_version so we can evolve envelope.

deploy-bot: staged canary rollout started cohort=canary-2 @1743220008

ops-bot: detected p95 tail increase in canary-2 @1743220020

ben: hysteresis: require probe_count >= 3 OR confidence >= 0.85 before escalating to QUIT. Manual override should short-circuit that.

zoe: question: how should router behave if decision publisher (arbiter) is unreachable? Cache last signed decision until ttl. If ttl expires, fall back to controller policy and emit a metric/alert.

ira: add kill-switch: router should track mismatch_count between arbiter and controller; if mismatch_rate > 1% over 5m, auto-ignore arbiter and fail open to controller (with paging).

ben: KV/streaming caution: QUIT must not forcibly close streams. Instead QUIT = refuse NEW session binds; if a stream exceeds a safety cap, route-broker should return 503 for new attach attempts rather than terminating.

zoe: operational playbook idea: 1) mirror arbiter decisions into controller for 24h; 2) run diff job; 3) opt-in tenant when diffs < threshold; 4) promote. Include CLI to force-ignore arbiter per-tenant.

ira: logging: every request should add headers decision_id and signer_version so traces can be correlated. Expose a query to list active binds for tenant+variant for audits.

ben: security: sign envelopes (JWT) and rotate signer keys monthly. Also include rollout_heartbeat metric so we can detect silent arbiter failure.

zoe: I'll fold this into the RFC: envelope spec, router lane semantics, cache/ttl rules, kill-switch thresholds, migration checklist, and sample curl/jq examples. Closing thread - will post RFC to #eng-platform tomorrow.

ira: :thumbsup: thanks.
